In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new methods for the design of digital circuits, and in particular the design of digital phase-locked loops (PLLs).
a fully synthesizable PLL that occupies a very small layout area, consumes low power and achieves a high phase noise.
the design of a new class of digital PLLs, which we call interpolative digital PLLs (i-DPLLS).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the proposed PLL is the smallest all-digital PLL (ADPLL) with injection-locked interpolative phase-couple oscillator, current output digital-toanalog converter (DAC) and fine-resolution digital varactor reported so far.
the proposed work is a highly efficient PLL design, and it is the first PLL to achieve such a high level of integration and small size using a digital design flow.
this paper presents a fully digital PLL with the smallest reported area to date, while achieving a very low phase noise and low jitter.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
this work achieves an area of 110 μm2 (65 nm CMOS), power of 780 μW, jitter of 1.7ps RMS (900MHz output), phase noise of -110 dBc/Hz (1MHz offset) and FOM of 187.5 dB.
this work achieves the best performance and the smallest area for the fully synthesizable PLL reported so far.
the proposed PLL is the first all-digital PLL that can be automatically P&R by a standard digital design flow.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the digital PLL design can be implemented using standard cells without manual intervention.
digital standard cells can be used to implement a PLL that can operate with a very low phase noise and low power consumption.
the digital PLL design flow is fully compatible with standard digital CMOS processes and design tools.
